title: Correctness when no estimate fails
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$, and let $0<\tau\le1$. For any outcome in the support of the Goldreich–Levin query program run against $f$, if its estimate trace contains no inaccurate record (each record's estimate differs from the corresponding restricted Fourier weight by less than $\tau^2/4$), then the outcome's state is correct: its active family exists, contains every $U$ with $\tau\le|\widehat f(U)|$, contains only sets with $\tau/2<|\widehat f(U)|$, and has cardinality at most both $\lceil4/\tau^2\rceil$ and $4/\tau^2$.
hypotheses_covered: The outcome belongs to the support of the program's output distribution
The outcome's trace has no record whose estimate differs from the associated restricted Fourier weight by at least $\tau^2/4$
